key_results: Verdict: across every null, the only robust excess is the spin (B1) redshift curvature, and with it the 16-dim magnetic block. E2, B2 and glide sit inside the null bulk. Removing patches 8 and 47 changes none of this. Because the nulls are randomizations of real rows, not independent mocks, this is a working diagnostic: calibrated_p = None, significance = None, physical_Pi = None, physical_GF = None.

Replay checks. R105 is replayed exactly: |Δ| ≤ 4.5e-13 on every R105 quadratic form (joint 406.385, magnetic 171.981, electric 16.826, magnetic rows without cross-covariance 52.131; delete-two joint 396.615). Re-accumulating the R98 shell×patch normal equations from the 634,233 source rows matches the cache to a max relative difference of 1.57e-15 (F) and 2.60e-15 (s). Injecting an affine-in-z frame into the RHS changes the curvature by at most 3.4e-14 (48 patches) and 3.2e-14 (46 patches) μas/yr/z².

Excluding patches 8 and 47. Patch centres (ICRS, deg): 8 at (202.5, +41.8) and 47 at (315.0, −66.4). Shell source counts drop from 92,686/238,552/174,944/128,051 to 87,403/224,704/164,465/119,991. Delete-one quadratic forms, all 48 patches → without 8 and 47: joint 32-dim 406.39 → 762.99; magnetic 16-dim (cross-row covariance kept) 171.98 → 199.85; electric 16-dim 16.83 → 17.27; magnetic given electric 389.56 → 745.72; spin6 104.12 → 103.19; B2_10 6.64 → 13.97; E2_10 5.38 → 3.86; glide6 8.28 → 7.60; magnetic rows without cross-covariance 52.13 → 61.94. Delete-two: joint 396.61 → 694.53, magnetic 169.83 → 195.85.

Why the joint form nearly doubles: the covariance changed, not the curvature vector. The shift of the 32-dim curvature vector caused by the exclusion gives a quadratic form of only 1.93 under the 48-patch delete-one covariance. Per-sector shift norms, row 0 / row 1 (μas/yr/z²): glide 5.88/3.66, spin 3.73/2.15, E2 11.47/7.44, B2 10.08/8.19. Meanwhile the covariance condition number rises from 722.9 to 1107.4 and the largest electric–magnetic canonical correlation from 0.958 to 0.968.

Curvature norms, row 0 / row 1 (μas/yr/z²). All 48 patches: spin 31.56/26.83, E2 23.44/12.11, B2 14.34/19.10, glide 11.21/10.30. Without 8 and 47: spin 33.95/27.78, E2 21.97/8.15, B2 18.60/23.37, glide 12.21/12.03. Per-shell spin magnitude (all 48 patches, shells z0–z3): 8.16, 3.20, 7.87, 5.23 μas/yr; the x component is −6.63, +2.13, +7.30, +1.95 μas/yr, i.e. it changes non-monotonically with z.

Nulls used, all through the identical estimator, the same exclusion and the same jackknife. (1) patch: redshift labels permuted inside each NSIDE-2 patch; 1000 draws; 71.97% of labels change. (2) patch_gmag: inside patch × 8 G-magnitude quantiles; 1000 draws; 71.55% change. (3) patch_gmag_colour: inside patch × 4 G × 4 BP−RP strata (768 strata); 2000 draws; 69.73% change. Every Quaia source has a CRF3 bp_rp value. (4) crf3_complement: 31,449 Gaia-CRF3 sources disjoint from Quaia G<20, with the same quality cuts and G between 13.88 and 20.00, given pseudo-shells from the Quaia shell fractions per stratum; 1000 draws. (5) crf3_complement_all_g: 580,531 disjoint CRF3 sources, median G 20.34, shells from Quaia fractions per patch × colour; 1000 draws.

spin6 against the nulls. Observed 104.12 (all 48) and 103.19 (without 8 and 47). Null 99th percentiles: 21.4 / 27.0 / 34.9 / 19.6 / 17.8 for nulls 1–5. None of the 6000 draws in either configuration reaches the observed value; the largest null value is 61.7. The magnetic 16-dim form behaves the same way: none of the 6000 draws reaches it, and its null 99th percentiles are 58.9–90.4. The idealized iid-patch Hotelling reference for spin6 is mean 7.05 and 99th percentile 21.9.

Joint 32-dim against the nulls (count of draws ≥ observed). All 48 patches (observed 406.39): 20/1000, 21/1000, 82/2000, 4/1000, 6/1000. Without 8 and 47 (observed 762.99): 6/1000, 1/1000, 18/2000, 0/1000, 0/1000. The same-source null tails are heavier than the Hotelling reference: 99th percentiles 496–612 versus 290 (48 patches) and 342 (46 patches).

E2_10, B2_10, glide6 and electric16 are within the null bulk in both configurations (between 23% and 96% of draws ≥ observed). The doubling of B2_10 on exclusion (ratio 2.10) lies in the upper tail of the null exclusion ratios (draws ≥ ratio: 14/1000, 9/1000, 17/2000, 1/1000, 2/1000), but the value after exclusion, 13.97, sits near the null median of about 11.

Systematics carried by the colour/magnitude-stratified null. Its mean spin curvature is 7.53/9.88 μas/yr/z² (row 0 / row 1), against 31.56/26.83 observed. Under that null's own 32-dim ensemble covariance, the null mean gives a quadratic of 7.25 and the observed-minus-null-mean vector gives 210.96. So magnitude and colour composition carry only part of the spin curvature. Permutation-ensemble RMS for spin (8.1/7.3) is smaller than the patch-jackknife RMS (12.19/9.11).

Classification of the result. Physical attribution: none. Conditional diagnostic: spin curvature depends on z in a way not exchangeable within sky × G × BP−RP strata. Possible causes not separated here include redshift-correlated AGN/host centroid effects, the scan law, and chromaticity beyond BP−RP. Numerical: R105 replay and source replay match to machine precision.

Gaps in the record. The null receipts do not store the SHA of quaia_gaia_full_join.npz; it was used only to exclude Quaia IDs from the complement, and I hashed it afterwards: 4cd83b1e8bb9f71f89aacfc2db5daba87f9a79f2af8ccd2e7e94b0be57252dae. The null ensembles ran under code SHA 72b1e19f4457119775ddcd9521b984a65d2db23399b820aa49a968e194f1db32. The final file (9dd338268206c950caff6fbc6a234a505a4ad2de5e58b44b26628cc0e612189b) differs only in summarize() and observed(); null() was not edited. No tracked file was edited (git shows only the untracked scripts/r106/).
tasks.classification: conditional prediction (working diagnostic only, no physical attribution). The R105/R98 replay matches to machine precision. Not converted to a significance: no independent-mock calibration exists.
blockers: No independent mock ensemble exists for the Gaia/Quaia curvature estimator: no release-calibrated AGIS scan-correlated error law and no independent AGN photocentre control sample (R100/R101 D04 = BLOCKED_DATA). All nulls here are randomizations of one real noise realization, so neither a significance nor a calibrated p can be produced.

The R105 handoff asks for an 'independent frame/sky null' but names no catalogue or mock set; none was found in the R98–R105 docs. The CRF3 complement inside the Quaia G range has only 31,449 sources (5% of Quaia), and the all-G complement is mostly fainter than Quaia (median G 20.34), so neither is fully magnitude-matched.

A physical interpretation of the spin (B1) curvature needs controls that are not available: an independent AGN-centroid/host sample, a chromaticity calibration beyond BP−RP, and a scan-law model. physical_Pi and physical_GF stay None.

tasks.task: D3: build an independent LSS/selection null for the NVSS integrated-minus-peak contrast and evaluate it with the identical R65 estimator. The estimator is the peak-integrated nonlinear common-transverse fit: ring-conditioned multinomial, fit_joint/shared_maps, common_influences + source_overlap_sandwich. It runs on the SHA-pinned provider catalogue with the R65 NSIDE=64 mask (33,000 pixels) and the R105 deletion blocks (166 at NSIDE=4, 594 at NSIDE=8). Each mock is a Cox process that keeps the footprint's actual flux pairs and adds provider-sigma flux scatter. It uses lognormal fields with amplitudes fitted to the data's own block-jackknife traces. The report gives the null distribution of the Wald statistic and the observed rank. No committed R65 or R105 file was written.

key_results: Mocks actually completed in the final run: 2000 per family x 4 families = 8000 full R65 refits, each with both the dipole and dipole_stf models. Also run: 108 NSIDE=4 block-jackknife calibration mocks (12 per amplitude level), 36 shape-diagnostic mocks with both NSIDE=4 and NSIDE=8 jackknifes (9 per family), and 3 timing mocks. Total compute wall time across all 5 commands: 1033.6 s (final run 785.66 s). Peak RSS of the largest single process: 388,028 kB. Workers: 3.

The R65 statistic replays exactly from the raw catalogue and the carrier. Dipole: delta(int-peak) = (-1.39604e-3, +5.62704e-3), Wald 32.7924; maximum delta error vs R65 = 6.1e-16; relative Wald error = 9.9e-14. dipole_stf: Wald 30.9895, identical to R65. The raw-to-joint-carrier replay is bitwise equal.

Data targets from R105 for the dipole model. Single-selection jackknife trace (peak + integrated): NSIDE=4 7.166e-5, NSIDE=8 5.627e-5, ratio 0.785. Contrast jackknife trace: NSIDE=4 6.815e-6, NSIDE=8 4.633e-6, ratio 0.680. R65 Poisson contrast trace: 1.814e-6 (dipole).

LSS_COMMON: one shared lognormal field, C_l = A_c l^-1.2 with A_c = 2.517e-4, fitted so the mock NSIDE=4 single-selection jackknife trace is 7.176e-5 +- 0.17e-5, matching the target. This family reproduces neither the contrast jackknife trace (1.99e-6 vs 6.815e-6) nor the pixel overdispersion (mock 1.008/1.009 vs data 1.064/1.104), so the data reject it as a null. Under it, contrast covariance = 0.98x R65 Poisson, and 0 of 2000 mocks reach the observed Wald 32.79 (dipole) or 30.99 (stf), giving p_MC = 1/2001 = 5.0e-4 (the resolution limit). A shared LSS field cancels in the contrast.

Differential-field families: an extra independent lognormal field acts on the off-diagonal (resolved/migrating) joint classes. Its amplitude is fitted so the mock NSIDE=4 contrast jackknife trace matches 6.815e-6 (achieved 6.77e-6, 6.62e-6 and 6.78e-6). The angular shape is assumed per family and then checked against the data's NSIDE=8/NSIDE=4 contrast jackknife ratio, which is 0.680.

LSS_DIFF_MID (C_l = A_m l^-0.6, A_m = 4.562e-3) is the shape the data's own diagnostics prefer. Contrast jackknife ratio NSIDE=8/NSIDE=4 = 0.712 +- 0.022 (data 0.680). Single-selection ratio = 0.774 +- 0.031 (data 0.785). Unfitted pixel overdispersion: integrated 1.090 vs data 1.104, peak 1.033 vs data 1.064. The ensemble contrast covariance is 9.2x R65 Poisson and 2.45x the data's NSIDE=4 jackknife.

LSS_DIFF_MID null result. Dipole: 335 of 2000 mocks have R65 Wald >= 32.79 (rank 336, p_MC = 0.168; mock median 12.8, 95th percentile 53.5). dipole_stf: 359/2000 reach 30.99 (rank 360, p_MC = 0.180). R105 jackknife covariances held fixed, NSIDE=4: observed 7.87, p_MC = 0.295. Same, NSIDE=8: observed 11.58, p_MC = 0.255. Observed Wald under the mock-ensemble covariance: 3.73, p_MC = 0.154.

LSS_DIFF_FLAT (C_l = A_m for l <= 48, A_m = 1.270e-3) is too white: contrast ratio 0.848 +- 0.035 vs 0.680, about 4.9 sigma off. Dipole: 23/2000 reach 32.79, p_MC = 0.012. dipole_stf: p_MC = 0.0155. Fixed jackknife NSIDE=4 covariance: p_MC = 0.051. Ensemble contrast covariance = 3.74x Poisson and 1.00x the data's NSIDE=4 jackknife.

LSS_DIFF_RED (C_l = A_m l^-1.2, A_m = 1.822e-2) is too red: contrast ratio 0.583 +- 0.022 vs 0.680, about 4.5 sigma off; single-selection ratio 0.696 +- 0.026 vs 0.785. Dipole: 1134/2000 reach 32.79, p_MC = 0.567. dipole_stf: p_MC = 0.569. Ensemble contrast covariance = 28.8x Poisson and 7.65x the data's NSIDE=4 jackknife.

Per-mock R105 statistic (each mock's own NSIDE=4 jackknife Wald), 9 mocks per family. MID: 1/9 reach 7.87 (p = 0.2). FLAT: 0/9 (p = 0.1). COMMON: 0/9 (p = 0.1). RED: 6/9 (p = 0.7). This is coarse at 9 mocks.

Mean mock contrast is consistent with zero, as the construction requires. For example, MID dipole mean = (3.1e-5 +- 6.2e-5, -3.7e-5 +- 6.7e-5). The largest deviation is RED y = -2.6e-4 +- 1.17e-4 (2.2 sigma, one of 16 components).

Interpretation: the R65 Poisson Wald (p ~ 7.6e-8 under chi2 df 2) is not a calibrated significance. Under nulls whose differential clustering reproduces the data's own contrast jackknife variance, p_MC ranges from 0.012 to 0.57 depending on the assumed angular shape. The shape preferred by the data's own two-scale jackknife ratio gives p_MC ~ 0.17-0.18. The integrated-minus-peak contrast is therefore not significant beyond plausible resolved-population clustering. This is a conditional calibration, not a physical attribution.

key_results: CF3 availability: the original VizieR J/AJ/152/50 table3.dat is NOT on disk (17,669 rows; 7,191,283 B; SHA-256 8acd4718ffe370e58d9747ffa3d8aeafcf3f554c698c82c00f29f5dec270aa19). Its recorded path /home/cosmosapjw/.cache/htt-r9/cf3_tempel_2017/CF3_table3.dat no longer exists, and it was not found in the repo or /mnt/extdrive/workdir/raw. Used instead: the CF3 copy shipped in the CORAS donor (commit 45ab256): CF3_group_member_catalog.dat (17,647 galaxies, SHA a776865717eb...) and CF3_group_catalog.dat (11,500 nests including singletons, SHA ad457eec5ca6...). Because table3 is missing, CF3's own per-galaxy method letters (r_Dist P/I/H/F/N/S/T/C/L/M) are unavailable; method attribution uses CF4 table2 per-method moduli for the same PGC.

6dFGSv vs CF3: 8,878 of 8,885 6dFGSv rows are CF3 members. Sky+CMB-cz route (15 arcsec, 500 km/s; median separation 0.44 arcsec): 8,864 matched. PGC route via the CF4 R103 match: 7,193. The two routes agree on all 7,179 rows matched by both (0 disagree); position-only 1,685, PGC-only 14, unmatched 7. All 7,190 R105-selected marks are CF3 members. For 8,620 of 8,878 the CF3 mu error is exactly 0.50 mag, which matches CF3's fixed e_DM-P for 6dF FP distances. CF4 method flags of these galaxies: FP 7,111, TF 133, SBF 38, SNIa 36, SNII 5, TRGB 1; 1,684 have no CF4 row.

CF4 galaxies that are CF3 members (exact PGC match), by method: all 15,823 of 55,877; FP 8,440 of 42,223 (6dFGSv FP 7,110 of 7,111; SDSS-PV FP 251 of 34,000; other FP 1,079 of 1,112); TF 6,703 of 12,222; SNIa 467 of 1,004; SBF 416 of 469; SNII 45 of 94; TRGB 291 of 446; Cepheid 60 of 69; Maser 3 of 6.

R98 CF4 groups: 8,945 of the 35,970 selected groups contain a CF3 member, and 4,980 contain a 6dFGSv galaxy. In the 21,860 groups covered by the 2MRS field: 8,880 with a CF3 member, 4,980 with a 6dFGSv galaxy. In the 14,110 missing groups: 65 with a CF3 member, 0 with a 6dFGSv galaxy. By method in the selected groups: FP-6dFGSv groups 4,915, all with a CF3 FP member; SDSS-FP groups 22,624, of which 56 have a CF3 SDSS-FP member; TF groups 8,463 (4,031 with a CF3 TF member); SNIa 851 (367).

CORAS calibration lineage: CORAS fixes f sigma8 = 0.405, external bulk (95, -172, 28) km/s and h = 0.7499. These come from the calibrated row rs = 15 Mpc/h, czMin = 2000 km/s, fitted on CF3 groups with 2,000-16,000 km/s: f sigma8 = 0.40502 +/- 0.06662, bulk (95.37, -172.43, 27.85) km/s, h = 0.74991. CF3 groups in that window: 10,319 (CMB frame) and 10,226 (LG frame) of 11,500. 6dFGSv rows whose CF3 group lies in the window: 8,627 (CMB), 8,575 (LG), 8,725 in either frame, 8,477 in both. Only 160 rows (120 R105-selected) are outside the window in both frames or not in CF3. The 6dFGSv-attributable share of the window's distance-modulus inverse variance is 0.407 (CMB) / 0.409 (LG); the share of velocity-error inverse variance is 0.172 / 0.181. These window counts are taken before CORAS's 5-sigma clip, so they are a superset of the objects actually used in calibration.

2MRS galaxies used by CORAS vs the 6dFGSv held-out galaxies: the reproduced CORAS pilot cut (CMB frame, Ks <= 11.754, partial volume limit M <= -20.624, R <= 200 Mpc/h) keeps 42,701 of 44,572 real 2MRS galaxies. The pilot log reports 46,876 selected, which implies 4,175 zone-of-avoidance clones (not independently verified). 3,983 of 8,885 6dFGSv rows are the same object as a 2MRS galaxy (sky+cz; median separation 0.25 arcsec, 99th percentile 0.72 arcsec). The 2MASS/6dF designation route agrees on 3,982 with 0 disagreements. All 3,983 are in the CORAS input, including 3,230 of the 7,190 R105-selected marks; example: PGC fold 0 has 824 of 1,777 test rows (656 of 1,442 selected). 8,226 of 17,647 CF3 galaxies are themselves CORAS 2MRS tracers.

Common zero points: CF3 mu minus mu_6dF (H0 = 75, Om = 0.3) has median -0.0062 mag, robust sd 0.0323 mag, rms 0.1035 mag (n = 8,878); Hubble-residual Pearson correlation 0.983. CF4 DMfp minus CF3 mu: median -0.034 mag, robust sd 0.030 mag (n = 7,111), Pearson 0.984. CF4 DMfp minus mu_6dF: median -0.0475 mag. At the median cz of 11,576 km/s these equal -33, -181 and -253 km/s. CF4 single-method minus CF3: TF -0.075 mag (n = 6,396), FP -0.034 (8,194), SNIa -0.027 (253), TRGB -0.050 (210), SBF +0.034 (233). Conclusion: one set of 6dF FP measurements, shifted by zero points, appears in all three catalogues; they are not independent samples.

6dFGSv delta_d split: 2MRS members minus non-members at matched cz is +0.0988 +/- 0.0028 dex (0.494 mag). It falls from 0.222 dex at 4,000-6,000 km/s to 0.078 dex at 14,000-16,000 km/s. This is apparent-K-magnitude selection acting on the mark itself. By contrast, CF3-window minus outside is -0.0099 +/- 0.0118 dex, consistent with zero, so the CF3 split is not confounded this way.

Replay: the R105 relative scores are reproduced exactly before any exclusion. Field holdout maximum fold error 3.3e-12; CORAS 8 draws (r24/l4/fft16) 0.0; CORAS 128 draws (r36/l8/fft24, R106 marks128) 0.0 against CF4_MARKS128.json. Full PGC/PGC1 sums: fixed_2mrs_offset 47.869/47.885 nats; CORAS-8 mean_offset 72.793/72.797; CORAS-128 draws_offset 78.588/79.231.

Rescore with CF3 overlap excluded: excluding all CF3 members leaves 7 rows and 0 selected marks, so no rescoring is possible. Excluding the CF3 calibration window keeps 160 rows (120 selected). On those, scoring only the held-out rows (training unchanged), PGC/PGC1: NN fixed_2mrs +1.65/+1.65 nats vs control 2.01+/-1.18 / 0.13+/-1.14. CORAS-128 draws+offset minus offset-only +5.00/+5.93 vs 5.96+/-0.88 / 4.85+/-1.19 (F = 0.09/0.82, where F is the fraction of controls <= observed). CORAS-8 mean+offset minus offset-only +3.74/+4.78. Removing the rows from both training and test sets: CORAS-128 draws minus offset +3.25/+3.24 vs 3.19+/-0.94 / 3.17+/-0.98. All are consistent with matched controls, but power is low (control sd about 1 nat).

Rescore with 2MRS tracers excluded (4,902 rows, 3,960 selected kept), test rows only, PGC/PGC1: offset_only -39.45/-39.12 (control +16.59/+18.25, sd about 3.2); fixed_2mrs -3.47/-3.45 (control +14.09/+13.46); CORAS-8 mean_offset -46.62/-46.69 (control +29.75/+29.85); CORAS-128 draws_offset -44.97/-44.35 (control +32.75/+33.14). In every case F = 0 of 2,000 controls; this is driven by the +0.099 dex zero point. Removed from both training and test sets: offset_only +79.35/+79.34; field minus offset: NN -0.77/-0.71 (control +8.48+/-3.03), CORAS-8 mean -7.57/-7.55, CORAS-128 draws +11.12/+11.15 (control 12.31+/-2.68, F = 0.28/0.34).

Recentred sensitivity (outside the R105 model set; the mark zero point is fitted on training rows): on the full sample NN fixed_2mrs drops 25.50 -> 17.93 and offset_only 25.24 -> 3.82, so these parts of the R105 scores are zero-point absorption. CORAS-128 draws minus offset becomes +38.60/+39.20. On non-2MRS galaxies only: NN +9.04/+8.83 (control 8.18+/-2.74 / 7.91+/-2.72); CORAS-8 mean +12.09/+12.35 (control 11.13 / 10.74); CORAS-128 draws +19.18/+19.18 (control 12.60+/-2.24 / 11.99+/-2.28; above all 32 controls). So there is no evidence that the field gain depends on a galaxy being a CORAS/NN tracer.

Union keep-set (120 rows, 87 selected; neither a 2MRS tracer nor in the CF3 window): CORAS field minus offset is -0.22 to -0.72 nats vs controls of +0.0 to +0.3, below all 32 drop controls; test-only F = 0.0005-0.18. NN is -0.02 to +0.12 vs about 0.8. Tiny sample, reported without a calibrated p-value.

Scope: Q and the predictive gain must stay conditioned on sample overlap. 100% of selected marks share their measurement with CF3. At least 98.2% (8,725 of 8,885) sit in CF3 groups inside the window that fixed CORAS's growth rate and bulk flow. Independence from the CF3 calibration is bounded only by the 160-row exclusion; it has not been removed.
tasks.classification: This is a conditional prediction, not a physical attribution or a numerical-convergence result. The rescoring gives working-model relative log predictive scores on the R105 folds, with no calibrated p-value and no physical Pi/G_F, H0-axis or Bianchi claim. The overlap counts and calibration-window figures are sample-lineage bookkeeping only. The only numerical check is the exact replay of the R105 scores before any exclusion.
blockers: Missing input: VizieR J/AJ/152/50 table3.dat (Cosmicflows-3, 17,669 rows, 7,191,283 B, SHA-256 8acd4718ffe370e58d9747ffa3d8aeafcf3f554c698c82c00f29f5dec270aa19, https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/ftp/J/AJ/152/50/table3.dat). Its recorded location /home/cosmosapjw/.cache/htt-r9/cf3_tempel_2017/CF3_table3.dat is absent. Without it, CF3's internal source letters (r_Dist), o_Dist, DM-P/e_DM-P (6dF with the CF3 zero point), DM-I, DM-N, DM-CF2 and Ksmag cannot be used. Method attribution falls back on CF4 table2 for the same PGC.

CORAS's 5-sigma outlier clip in prepare_distance_catalog_data needs the fiducial 5 Mpc/h reconstruction from estimate_parameters.x, which was not run. The CF3 calibration-window membership (8,725 rows in either frame) is therefore a superset of actual calibration use.

f sigma8 and the external bulk were not recalibrated on CF3 minus 6dFGSv; that needs estimate_parameters.x with 50 constrained realisations at full resolution, which was not attempted within the 3-worker / 6 GB limit. The leakage of 6dF labels into the fixed CORAS calibration can only be bounded by the 160-row exclusion, not removed.

No local K-band magnitudes exist for the 4,902 non-2MRS 6dFGSv rows (6dFGS photometry, or CF3 table3 Ksmag). A luminosity-matched control is therefore impossible; the 2MRS split is confounded with the +0.0988 dex apparent-magnitude zero point.
Drop and recentred controls use 32 replicates, so F has a resolution of 1/32. Test-only controls use 2,000 replicates.
